title: Gordan lemma for lattice points in a rational cone
statement: Let $L$ be a free abelian group of finite rank, that is, an abelian group with elements $e_1,\ldots,e_d$ such that every element of $L$ is uniquely $\sum_j m_je_j$ with $m_j\in\mathbf Z$; regard $L\subseteq L\otimes_{\mathbf Z}\mathbf Q$. Let $v_1,\ldots,v_r\in L$, allowing $r=0$. Put $C=\{\sum_i q_i v_i:q_i\in\mathbf Q_{\ge 0}\}\subseteq L\otimes_{\mathbf Z}\mathbf Q$ and $P=\{\sum_i n_i v_i:n_i\in\mathbf N\}\subseteq L$. Then there is a finite set $F\subseteq C\cap L$ such that $C\cap L=\bigcup_{f\in F}(f+P)$. In particular, $C\cap L$ is a finitely generated commutative monoid, generated by $F$ and $v_1,\ldots,v_r$.

source.place: Expose VIII, 3.2.9, proof, printed p. 104 (finite toric saturation); expanded as the standard fundamental-parallelepiped proof of Gordan's lemma.
